# An actual face bulge has a tent-weighted incidence cost

This planar theorem allows the visible face to cross several original
cap-sign regions. It retains the actual common body, its compatible
enlargement room, all competing integer fibers, and the whole visible
face. The remainder is proved to be o(epsilon) for a general convex
body; no uniform quadratic remainder at arbitrarily flat curved joins
is asserted.

## 1. Compatible geometric variation

Use the planar three-fiber setting, fixed caps, and notation from
`candidate 9d3ac163e4b5a3f7`.
Thus A,K,B are convex bodies, (A+B)/2 subset K, the source y_0 is in
int K, and three normals v_i sum to zero and span the plane. Their
equal-mass Q caps have proper A and K traces and supporting B traces.
Write b_i=2v_i.y_0-h_B(v_i), s_i=2sigma_Ai+sigma_Ki,
lambda_i=1/s_i, Lambda=sum lambda_i, and p_i=lambda_i/Lambda.

Let F be a nondegenerate exposed line segment of A, taken to be the
WHOLE supporting face on its line. Let E={x:x+B subset 2K}.
Suppose p belongs to relint F and to int E. Let n be the outward unit
normal to F. For sufficiently small epsilon>0 define

    A_epsilon=conv(A union {p+epsilon n}).             (1)

It is an actual convex body containing A and contained in E, so
(A_epsilon+B)/2 subset K. K and B are unchanged. The three labeled
fibers again form the exact integer sections of an actual convex body.

Choose orthonormal coordinates in which F=[alpha,beta] times {0},
A lies below its supporting line, and p=(t,0), alpha<t<beta. Define
the unit-height tent on F by

    T_t(s)=(s-alpha)/(t-alpha),       alpha<=s<=t,
           (beta-s)/(beta-t),        t<=s<=beta.       (2)

For each original proper A cap H_i^A={x:v_i.x>=b_i}, the exact
first-order formula is

    |(A_epsilon minus A) intersect H_i^A|
       =epsilon c_i(t)+o(epsilon),
    c_i(t)=integral_alpha^beta T_t(s)
                       1_(H_i^A)(s,0) ds.            (3)

The total added area is

    delta_epsilon=epsilon(beta-alpha)/2+o(epsilon).  (4)

## 2. Complete control of the visible-face remainder

Let f(s) be the upper boundary of A on its horizontal projection.
It is concave, has maximum 0, and its zero set is exactly [alpha,beta].
The upper boundary g_epsilon of the hull with (t,epsilon) joins this
point on its two sides to the old boundary by supporting line segments.
Write a_epsilon<=alpha and b_epsilon>=beta for their contact
coordinates. For example, the left contact minimizes
(epsilon-f(s))/(t-s) over s<=alpha; the corresponding positive quotient
on the right is treated the same way. The denominators are bounded
away from zero, and upper semicontinuity of the closed body's upper
boundary makes these quotients lower semicontinuous on compact
domains, so their minima are attained.
If a supporting segment coincides with an old straight edge, use its
furthest contact in that direction. No differentiability of f is used.

The nonnegative slope m_epsilon of the left segment is at most
epsilon/(t-alpha), because its line lies above (alpha,0). At contact,

    0<=-f(a_epsilon)
       <=epsilon(alpha-a_epsilon)/(t-alpha).         (5)

The contact heights tend to zero. Compactness of A implies that
any limit contact lies in F; hence a_epsilon tends to alpha. Thus
f(a_epsilon)=o(epsilon) and

    m_epsilon/epsilon ->1/(t-alpha).

The same argument holds on the right. Consequently g_epsilon/epsilon
converges uniformly on F to (2).

There is also a global height bound:

    A_epsilon subset A+[0,epsilon n],

since the convex set on the right contains A and the new point. Each
vertical section therefore gains upper height at most epsilon and
cannot gain below its old lower endpoint. Outside [alpha,beta] the
visible interval has length tending to zero, so its entire added area
is o(epsilon). The added part has vertical coordinates between its
two o(epsilon) contact heights and epsilon. Integrating on F proves
(4).

A proper A cutting line cannot contain the supporting segment F. Its
indicator on F has at most one discontinuity, unless it is constant.
Bounded convergence applied to the uniform tent limit gives (3).
This also holds uniformly when the cap threshold changes by
O(epsilon): on F a transverse cut then changes the indicator over
length O(epsilon), contributing O(epsilon^2) area, while the entire
outside-F contribution is already o(epsilon). A parallel proper cut
has positive separation from F and causes no change for small shifts.

For a polytope A, p in relint F strictly satisfies every other facet
inequality. The same holds for p+epsilon n for small epsilon. The
added set is then EXACTLY the triangle over F with that apex, with no
adjacent-edge correction. The preceding argument proves the needed
first-order formula without assuming polyhedrality.

## 3. One actual moving cap menu and all integer sources

Put

    F_i(y)=|K intersect {v_i.x>=v_i.y}|
       +|A intersect {v_i.x>=2v_i.y-h_B(v_i)}|.

These functions are C^1 near y_0, with gradients -s_i v_i, by
continuity of proper convex section lengths. Let Delta_i^epsilon(y)
be the added A_epsilon mass in that same moving A cap. Section 2 gives

    Delta_i^epsilon(y)=epsilon c_i(t)+o(epsilon)
          whenever |y-y_0|=O(epsilon).               (6)

There is an actual nearby meeting point and common budget satisfying

    F_i(y_epsilon)+Delta_i^epsilon(y_epsilon)
          =q_epsilon for every i,
    y_epsilon-y_0=O(epsilon),
    q_epsilon=Q+epsilon sum_i p_i c_i(t)+o(epsilon). (7)

Here is a full implicit-step justification without a differentiable
boundary family. The original map G(y,q)=(F_i(y)-q)_i is a local C^1
diffeomorphism: its Jacobian kernel is zero by multiplication with
1/s_i and use of sum v_i=0. The added-cap functions Delta_i^epsilon
are Lipschitz in y with constants tending to zero. Indeed, the added
region lies in a horizontal band of height epsilon+o(epsilon). A
cutting line transverse to F intersects such a band in length
O(epsilon), uniformly in its threshold; coarea bounds its cap-volume
change accordingly. For a parallel original cut there is no added
mass near the cutting LINE, so its added cap mass is locally constant
in the threshold (possibly the entire added area). Thus the constants
vanish uniformly in a fixed small
neighborhood of y_0, also at boundary crossing thresholds.

Use the local inverse of G in the equation

    (y,q)=G^(-1)(-Delta^epsilon(y)).

On a sufficiently large ball of radius O(epsilon) about (y_0,Q),
this map sends the ball into itself, since Delta^epsilon=O(epsilon)
and the inverse has bounded derivative. It is a contraction by the
vanishing Lipschitz estimate. Its actual fixed point has the stated
distance bound. Expand G to first order, use (6), and multiply the
equations by lambda_i and sum. This proves the last formula in (7).

The middle traces through y_epsilon cover the plane, so their common
budget bounds every middle-fiber depth. Assume Q is the original
GLOBAL raw maximum and the endpoint ordinary maximum m_A satisfies
m_A<Q. The unchanged endpoint may be tied: m_B<=Q. The new ordinary
A maximum is at most m_A+delta_epsilon, including newly added points,
by the all-continuous-point measure comparison proved in the strict-
signature source. Its gap persists. The coefficient in (7) is strictly
positive: the original A halfspaces cover the plane and all p_i>0.
Therefore q_epsilon>Q>=m_B as well for small epsilon. The new GLOBAL
maximum is at most q_epsilon, without any persistence assumption for
minimizing normals.

## 4. Exact tent cost and its finite evaluation

Write M=|A|+|K|+|B| and r=Q/M. On the ACTUAL face define

    W(s)=sum_i p_i 1_(H_i^A)(s,0),
    f_cost(s)=W(s)-r.

Then

    q_epsilon/(M+delta_epsilon)-Q/M
       =(epsilon/M) C(t)+o(epsilon),
    C(t)=integral_alpha^beta T_t(s) f_cost(s) ds.      (8)

Any available p=(t,0) in relint F intersect int E with C(t)<0
therefore gives genuine strict normalized-depth descent. It tests
the entire visible-face incidence, not just the signature at p. A
tied unchanged endpoint causes no additional condition.

This cost has an exact elementary evaluation. Put

    A(t)=integral_alpha^t (s-alpha) f_cost(s) ds,
    B(t)=integral_t^beta (beta-s) f_cost(s) ds.

Then

    C(t)=A(t)/(t-alpha)+B(t)/(beta-t),
    C'(t)=-A(t)/(t-alpha)^2+B(t)/(beta-t)^2.           (9)

Each cutting line meets F at most once, so there are at most three
cut breakpoints. On an interval between them with constant cost c,

    A(t)=c(t-alpha)^2/2+A_0,
    B(t)=c(beta-t)^2/2+B_0,
    C'(t)=-A_0/(t-alpha)^2+B_0/(beta-t)^2.            (10)

An interior stationary point requires A_0,B_0 to have the same sign
(or both vanish); otherwise there is none. When both are nonzero,
its position is given exactly by

    (t-alpha)/(beta-t)=sqrt(|A_0|/|B_0|).

Thus the cost can be checked at cut breakpoints, endpoints of the
available interval by continuity, and these explicit stationary points.
Availability still requires p in int E; a formal optimum without
compatible room is insufficient.

No assertion is made that C(t) must be negative on some available
face or that every low-weight unique corner has a freely expandable
boundary. The result supplies an exact actual variation and cost
for use with further common-body geometry.

## 5. A sharp interval concentration calculation for the actual tent

There is a useful explicit way to test one low-weight corner interval.
Normalize F to [0,1], and let [a,b] be an interval of relative length
ell=b-a. The normalized tent measure has density 2T_t(s). Then

    sup_(0<t<1) integral_a^b 2T_t(s) ds
       =1-(1-ell)^2=2ell-ell^2.                     (11)

For 0<a<b<1 the supremum is attained at the actual interior position
t_*=a/[a+(1-b)], which lies in [a,b]. To prove this, for t in [a,b]
the excluded mass is

    a^2/t+(1-b)^2/(1-t)
       >=[a+(1-b)]^2.

The inequality is the two-term Cauchy--Schwarz inequality, with
equality at t_*. If t<a the interval mass increases as t moves to a;
if t>b it increases as t moves back to b, by direct integration of
the one affine branch of the tent. Thus no outside peak improves the
value. Endpoint intervals have the same supremum by a one-sided
limit; the entire face has mass 1 for every peak.

Suppose the interval is an actual unique-capture portion of F with
constant weight p_i<r=Q/M. Let w_out be any valid upper bound for W
on its complement in the same face, with w_out>=r. At the optimizing
peak from (11), the mean incidence cost is at most

    w_out-r-(w_out-p_i)(2ell-ell^2).                 (12)

Consequently it is strictly negative whenever

    ell>1-sqrt((r-p_i)/(w_out-p_i)).                 (13)

This produces a genuine descent only if the optimizing peak lies in
int E; for an endpoint interval an available sequence of peaks
approaching that endpoint suffices when (13) is strict. One may always
take w_out=1, or use the smaller exact largest incidence weight on the
rest of that face. This is a sharp tent concentration computation,
not a claim that actual faces automatically have the required length
fraction or the required compatible room.

## 6. Exact support equality is the only compatibility barrier on a face

The availability condition can be made concrete for a relative-interior
point of this face. Let n be the outward unit normal of the whole face
F. Then, for ANY p in relint F,

    p in int E
      if and only if h_A(n)+h_B(n)<2h_K(n).          (14)

Actual midpoint compatibility always gives the weak inequality.
For proof, the feasible body has the exact representation

    E=intersection_(||u||=1)
          {x:u.x<=2h_K(u)-h_B(u)}.

If p lies on its boundary, at least one displayed constraint is
active. Otherwise its continuous slack function has a strictly
positive minimum on the compact unit sphere, putting a ball about p
inside E. An active u also supports A at p, since A subset E.
At a relative-interior point of a supporting segment, the only unit
supporting normal of A is n: the two directions along the segment
force the normal to be perpendicular to it, and the interior side of
A fixes the sign. Thus u=n and equality holds in (14). Conversely,
equality makes that constraint active at every p in F, so none lies
in int E. This proves the equivalence, including arbitrary nonsmooth
convex A,K,B.

Consequently, under the global-Q and m_A<Q assumptions, an ACTUAL
attained local minimum cannot have a face with a negative tent cost
and strict support slack. Every face with C(t)<0 at some relative-
interior position must instead obey the exact whole-body equality

    h_A(n)+h_B(n)=2h_K(n).                           (15)

Its actual exposed faces then satisfy

    (F_A(n)+F_B(n))/2 subset F_K(n),

by midpoint inclusion and equality of the support values. Since
F_A(n)=F has positive length, F_K(n) is also a positive-length face.
This converts the local obstruction to one concrete shared support
constraint. It does not classify all such faces or show that these
equalities are mutually incompatible.
